messages:
maya: Quick follow-ups from today's runtime roadmap segment 5. Thanks for the deep dive!
maya: 1) KV cache controls: customers asked if we can set hard residency limits per-tenant (regulated folks) or only soft/global heuristics.
taylor: Short plan: per-tenant policies coming to Private first, then Dedicated. Hosted keeps global heuristics + per-tenant soft caps for higher tiers.
taylor: Design: a soft residency TTL marks entries as evictable but still usable; a hard cap enforced by the memory controller if OOM risk.
alex: Technical nuance: soft TTLs let us avoid hot-key evictions during short bursts by degrading priority instead of immediate drop, which cuts tail p99 by ~12% in sims.
maya: 2) Batching signals: ops wants to know which percentiles we track for adaptive batching decisions. p99 vs p99.9? also sample frequency?
rami: We use p50/p90/p99/p99.9 for dashboarding. For automated batching decisions we currently experiment with p99.5 and p99.9 windows. Sampling rate is adjustable per-pool.
lucy: We tag latency samples with batch_size, seq_len, and route to build a latency-by-batch curve. That's what the autoscaler consults during contention.
sre-bot: [info] Sampling high-cardinality request tags increases metrics cardinality. Default sampling is 1%, can be raised for Dedicated customers.
maya: 3) Kernel pinning and compatibility: can customers pin kernels? How do we handle fallbacks for pinned kernels?
taylor: Yes, Dedicated alpha will support a kernel_profile field in the model manifest. Private will support through operator-managed mappings.
taylor: Fallback chain respects pinning: pinned -> compatible-quant -> generic. We also provide a compatibility-check endpoint so pinning is validated before commit.
alex: Addition: we will ship an "auto-tune" flag. If true, runtime can experiment with micro-kernel variants during low-traffic windows and report perf/cost tradeoffs.
maya: 4) Rollouts and regressions: leadership asked how we reconcile small latency regressions with large cost wins.
rami: Policy: auto-rollback triggers require exceeding both a latency SLO delta (configurable, e.g., +5ms at p99) and increases in error rate. Cost-only wins do not auto-rollback.
zach: For safety, we run a canary run (synthetic load ~10k requests) during rollout, and a quick perf check across seq buckets.
maya: 5) Prewarm & cold-starts: customers worried about KV warmup latency on bursty traffic. Any changes?
alex: New prewarm strategy snapshots hot KV segments to durable store and rehydrates on worker start. Also opportunistic prefix warming when traffic warms up.
alex: In internal tests that cut cold-path latency by ~30% for long-sequence workloads.
maya: 6) Customer controls for prewarm: can they pay to keep workers warmed / reserve prewarm budget?
taylor: Yes, Dedicated will expose a per-route "prewarm_budget" option. Hosted will expose a managed prewarm tier for enterprise customers.
maya: Small request from support: can eng publish a short RFC and a migration checklist for Dedicated customers who want to pin kernels or enable per-tenant TTLs?
taylor: I'll publish an RFC and a migration guide next week and link it here.
maya: Appreciated. Any blockers or unresolved action items?
rami: Action: alex to write perf regression thresholds doc. taylor to draft kernel pinning RFC. lucy to add sampling recommendations to console docs.
lucy: Will add console UI sketches for batch-latency curve and per-route prewarm settings.
maya: Thanks everyone, please ping me if you need anything before RFC drops. :thumbsup:
